tool.name: EWAS blocks (distance-aware HSMM)
tool.description: large-scale methylation blocks with calibrated boundaries, replacing cpgCollapse + blockFinder
tool.command: mkdir -p in out && ln -s '$mval' in/mval.f64 && ln -s '$dims' in/mval_dims.json && ln -s '$pheno' in/pheno_used.csv && ln -s '$anno' in/probe_annotation.csv && Rscript '$__tool_directory__/../bin/05_blocks_hsmm.R' --in-dir in --probe-map '$probe_map' --out-dir out --exposure '$design.exposure' --exposure-scale $design.exposure_scale --subject '$design.subject' --covars '$design.covars' --max-gap $cluster.max_gap --rho-min $cluster.rho_min --length-scale $hsmm.length_scale --min-post $hsmm.min_post --min-clusters $hsmm.min_clusters --seed $hsmm.seed #if $fixed_collapse --fixed-collapse #end if

param.name: probe_map
param.label: Cross-array probe map
param.help: crossarray_probe_map.csv.gz from the harmonisation tool. Supplies each probe's array status and island context, so blocks are restricted to open-sea probes that BOTH arrays carry.

section.name: cluster
section.title: Open-sea clustering (replaces the fixed 500 bp / 1500 bp collapse)

param.name: max_gap
param.label: Maximum genomic gap (bp) considered for joining

param.name: rho_min
param.label: Minimum within-subject co-methylation to join two open-sea probes

param.name: length_scale
param.label: Distance length scale L (bp)
param.help: Transition probabilities are A(d) = exp(-d/L) I + (1 - exp(-d/L)) 1 pi'. The 250 kb default matches the loess window it replaces, so the two are comparable.

param.name: min_post
param.label: Minimum posterior to include a cluster in a block
param.help: Blocks are decoded from the state posterior, so this is a probability, not an effect-size cutoff on a smooth curve.

param.name: fixed_collapse
param.label: Also report the legacy fixed-width collapse
param.help: Reports how many units, and of what width, the 500 bp gap / 1500 bp width rule would have produced on the same probes, so the change in the unit of analysis is visible.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Finds large-scale methylation blocks -- the megabase-scale hypo- and hypermethylated domains -- in a harmonised 450K + EPIC longitudinal study. It replaces section 2.7 of the minfi/EWASGalaxy stack: ``cpgCollapse`` with a fixed 500 bp gap / 1500 bp width rule, followed by ``blockFinder`` bump hunting with a 250 kb loess window.
**Why the original is not valid here**
Block finding runs on open-sea probes, and open sea is precisely the content that differs most between the two arrays: about 78% of EPIC-only probes are open sea against 36% of the probes both arrays share. A fixed-width collapse therefore builds units whose composition depends on which array a sample came from, which is exactly what a harmonisation pipeline must not do. Separately, the block boundary is wherever a wide loess curve crosses a cutoff; the minfi paper itself notes this makes boundaries resolution-limited, and it gives no measure of confidence in any particular boundary.
**What this tool does instead**
Clusters are formed where open-sea probes are both close and empirically co-methylated, restricted to probes both arrays carry, so a cluster is a property of the locus. Each cluster is collapsed to its mean profile and given a within-subject effect with its own standard error. A three-state hidden Markov model (hypo / neutral / hyper) then runs along the chromosome with a transition matrix that is an explicit function of genomic distance, so that two clusters 2 kb apart are strongly coupled and two clusters 5 Mb apart are effectively independent. Posterior decoding returns soft block boundaries with a per-block posterior probability, and the emission model uses each cluster's own standard error, so a noisy cluster cannot pull a boundary the way an unweighted smooth curve can.
@DESIGN_NOTE@
**Outputs**
A block table with per-block posterior, span, number of constituent clusters and direction; the per-cluster effect table with state posteriors; and the fitted model (state means, state standard deviations, stationary distribution, length scale, log-likelihood) plus the cross-array agreement of block effects between the two cohorts.
